SIMPLIFIED P&L BY MONTH, Q1 2026 (Harlow Dental Group PLLC) - built solely from bank operating-account activity (bank_operating_q1.csv / .pdf, 48 transactions, Jan 1 - Mar 31, 2026).

Conventions: revenue and expenses shown as positive magnitudes (expenses are outflows). Cash-basis from bank activity only; no accruals, no month-end adjusting entries.

Classification rules: revenue = the 12 MERCHANT DEPOSIT lines (Delta Dental / CIGNA / patient collections; insurer mix not separable from the statement). payroll = ACH ADP PAYROLL + ACH ADP TAX. supplies = ACH HENRY SCHEIN SUPPLIES + ACH PATTERSON DENTAL. rent = ACH PROPERTY MGMT RENT 3 LOCATIONS ($21,600.00 each month). other lines: utilities_austin_energy; software_dentrix ($1,290.00/month); summit_supply_checks_flagged = the 9 CHECK SUMMIT SUPPLY LLC disbursements ($4,900.00 or $4,950.00 each; $14,750.00/month; $44,250.00 total) - reported separately rather than in supplies because the supporting invoices (summit_supply_invoices.csv) describe several of these as 'consulting' with no deliverables identified on the file, and the disbursements are flagged as irregular (see below).

Open items (nothing forced to balance):
1) PAYROLL NOT RECONCILED: payroll_register_q1.csv gross_per_period sums to 65,576.15 per period (7 employees); x 6 pay dates = 393,456.90 gross for Q1, versus combined ADP debits of 673,050.48 (526,713.92 ADP PAYROLL + 146,336.56 ADP TAX). Difference 279,593.58 is unexplained with the documents provided; the register appears not to cover all paid employees, or debits include additional amounts (benefits, garnishments, third parties) that we cannot decompose from a bank statement. Left open; see QUESTIONS.md.
2) NEGATIVE OPERATING BALANCE: the account runs to -118,735.42 by Mar 31 (first negative 02/28 after the ADP TAX debit, -12,552.80). A fully listed operating account should not go negative; either the statement omits credits or the account has an overdraft facility. Revenue above may therefore be understated. Unresolved; see QUESTIONS.md.
3) The flagged Summit Supply payments ($44,250.00 in Q1) exhibit indicators listed in library:fraud_indicators_reference.md (amounts at 98%-99% of the $5,000 two-partner-approval threshold in the client's approval_policy.md (pattern consistent with the library's 'amounts structured just under an approval threshold' indicator; no intent asserted); sole approval by the Managing Partner; vendor created by the approver; no W-9 on file; no PO or receiving documents; sequential invoice numbering (SS-100 to SS-108) at 8-13-day intervals (median 10); vague descriptions; vendor address matching a relative of the Managing Partner per the HR emergency-contact file). Per engagement letter section 4 these matters are reported in writing to the Chair of the Partnership Finance Committee because they involve or may involve the Managing Partner: see communication_to_dr_r_patel.md. Payments to an unlicensed third party for 'consulting' with no deliverables may raise unlawful fee-splitting concerns under library:tx_dental_fee_splitting.md - context noted; this office makes no legal determination of fraud or illegality (library:ssars_responsibilities.md: not auditors; procedures not designed to detect fraud; no fraud conclusion drawn).

Assumptions (stated prominently): (a) all 12 merchant-deposit lines are operating collections, no non-patient credits exist; (b) every listed transaction is posted above once and only once (sums tie to the statement, supporting this); (c) bank-activity classification is the deliverable requested, so insurance receivables/payables, depreciation, patient A/R and payables accruals are NOT reflected; month totals are movements, not accrual-basis P&L results. No general ledger or trial balance was provided, so books-to-bank reconciliation was not possible.
